title: When gratitude feels thin
issueStatement: You may know gratitude matters, but the heart feels dulled by entitlement, fatigue, or what is still missing.
centralInsight: Gurbani deepens gratitude by moving through unworthiness, mercy, and Naam instead of through self-congratulation.
practicalReflection: Gratitude becomes truer when it stops being a performance of positivity and becomes recognition of mercy.
actionPrompt: Name one mercy beneath the surface event: guidance, restraint, sangat, forgiveness, or breath itself.

source.shortMeaning: Mercy, Guru, and Naam are the deeper structure of gratitude.
source.lifeApplication: Thankfulness here leads back into spiritual life, not only good feelings.

excerpts.explanation: This shabad gives gratitude depth by rooting it in mercy.

source.shortMeaning: Pain can re-open praise where comfort forgets.
source.lifeApplication: Gratitude sometimes grows after false securities are shaken.

excerpts.explanation: Guru Nanak reframes comfort and difficulty without flattening either.

source.shortMeaning: Steadiness makes room for gratitude beyond circumstance.
source.lifeApplication: A grateful heart is less ruled by praise, blame, pleasure, or pain.

excerpts.explanation: Gratitude gets sturdier when the mind is less hooked by swings.
